utterances.text: All right. Let's redact line 10 or -- line 10 and 11 of the -- of page 52, the words before, "they told," up to "shirt off." Then we can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You stated that there was a camera. Was there somebody operating this camera, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: Yes. I think that it was filmed. There was a cameraman on my right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If we may move again into private session, Your Honour, I think we can proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly. Let's move back to private session for a short while, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I want to turn your attention, Witness, back to the house that you've mentioned a couple of times. Can you just describe the appearance of the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: The house that was there on my right-hand side, looked as if it had been set on fire already. That's what it seemed to me, as I was passing it. It was on my right-hand side. I could see there was some steps there. That's it more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: After you passed the house, where did you go next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: Yes. When you pass the house, you reach the asphalt, and then you had to turn left. And then when you turned left. You crossed the ash fault, and then when you turn left, there was a meadow on your right-hand side where there were a lot of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What if anything did the men who were surrendering do with any back-packs or other belongings that they had carried with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: If you had a back-pack or something with you, you had to leave it before you reached the asphalt. I saw back packs on my right-hand side, on the -- where the house was. So in order to reach the meadow also, you had to leave everything that you had, either before you reached the asphalt or afterwards. In any case, before you reached the meadow.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And this meadow you've referred to, was it level with the road or was it at a different level with the road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: No. It wasn't level with the road. I think that it was at a different level. It's a little bit higher. There is a slight incline in order to reach it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: When you arrived at the meadow, can you estimate for the Trial Chamber approximately how many other people you saw there? I'm referring to Muslim men.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: I would think that there were between 900 to a thousand people there for sure. This is my own estimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you see any military vehicles in that area near the meadow?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: Yes. When you reached the meadow from the asphalt, on my left side there was a black tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall in which direction the barrel was pointed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: The barrel was pointed in the direction from which we had come, in the direction of the hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And was there a machine-gun mounted on this tank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And where was it pointed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: It was pointed at all of us, all of us who were in the meadow, all of us. There was a soldier manning it at all times, and he kept threatening constantly, "I'm going to kill you," and so on. And he was hurling insults.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you testified previously having seen a UN APC and soldiers wearing the what appeared to be to be blue UN helmets when you were being called on to surrender. Did you see any soldiers in UN helmets again after you came out of the woods?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: No. After I came to the meadow, I didn't see the APC any more, the blue helmets. There were others there wearing UN clothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what kind of UN clothing were you referring to, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: I think they had UNPROFOR armour -- bullet-proof vests.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you describe what those looked like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: Well, how can I describe it? You mean what they look like or the colour? It was a kind of a green and brown colour. I knew it -- I knew them well and I'm sure of what I'm saying. I could describe it with the assistance of a picture, if you have one.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We'll get to that later, sir. When you describe it as [French coming over the English channel.]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We are getting some French.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Much to Madam Fauveau's pleasure.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Some Maurice Chevalier, Your Honour. I'll try the next question again, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You described it as a kind of green and brown colour. Was this a camouflage, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: Yes. Camouflage, yes. It was a kind of light brown colour that was very prominent.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, how is it that you believe you're so familiar with the UN --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Yes, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't believe we have an appropriate translation. What I heard the witness said regarding the tone of brown colour was kafe na bojak meaning colour of coffee. And here we have a light brown. I believe it was quite the opposite of what he meant. It was very dark brown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The witness has heard what you have to say. If he wants to correct or explain it again or describe it again, it's up to him and up to you, Mr. Thayer. He's not our witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Witness, did you understand what Mr. President just clarified?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: Yes. Well, there is no need to explain. If you show me a picture, I can tell you exactly what I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, Witness, we will he do that. Simply the colour you identified on these flak jackets, was it a light brown or a dark brown or neither?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: Coffee coloured. I was talking about coffee coloured. I didn't say anything about light or dark. I may have done but does anyone remember? It was coffee coloured and green, all mixed together. They were mixed together, those colours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we can proceed. Come on. I wish we don't lose much time on these issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, how is it, sir, that you're so familiar with the UN flak jackets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: Well, you know, in Srebrenica, we were more than once in a situation where we had nothing to eat. As a boy, I went to the UNPROFOR points, check-points, to ask them to give me something to eat, because I was hungry, and we had nothing to eat. The situation was disastrous, and there were times when we had nothing to eat. So I had to go to UNPROFOR to ask them to give me some food to eat so I would survive. And the patrols that passed by, I had many close encounters with UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: At this time I'd ask for 65 ter 1583 to be displayed on e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you see an image on your screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you describe for the Trial Chamber what that depicts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: In fact, this picture shows where we came from the house, the house itself, and the place where we were all placed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think he should mark these places, the house and the location where -- which he's just referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's where I'm going next.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would have imagined so. Let's assist him, yeah. Go ahead. Ask him what you need to ask him, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, I'd ask to you take that stylus and if you would, just trace the path that you took as you emerged from the woods, past the house, and then ultimately to the location where you were held?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: Here, like this. This is where I went and this is where the tank was.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And next to, if you would, to the right of where you just indicated the tank was, can you just write the word "tank"? If you know it in English, in English; if not, in your own language, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if you would, would you just draw a larger circle to indicate the general area where you and the others were being held?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the place where the house was that I delay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If you would just write next to the circle you just drew the word house in English, if you know it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If he knows. If he doesn't he can write "kuca."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: In the lower corner would you write PW-127, please and today's date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Witness, if you could please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I -- I haven't seen him doing this. Usher, could you assist him please and explain to him where he needs to put PW-127? In any of the corners. It's not important if it's the left or the right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 127?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you. I think we can save this image now. And I would ask at this point that 65 ter number 1584 be displayed on e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't know if it's important for Mr. Thayer but he also asked for a date of the marking of this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. All right. I think we can do that. Witness, where you wrote PW-127, just below or above, could you also put today's date, please, which is 2nd November, 2/11/2006. All right. Okay. We can't do it now because we have already moved to the next picture. But anyway, we'll do it later or whenever. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you see an image on your screen now, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Would you describe what that depicts for the Trial Chamber, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: I see a house, a cemetery below the house, and a lot of litter, rubbish.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recognise that house, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And which house is this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: That's the house that we passed by on that day we were taken prisoner.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you indicated, sir, that you passed it on your right; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: Yes. It was to my right, or, rather, looking at it from this direction, it's on the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you -- we'll just clarify this right now. If you just take the stylus, sir, and please indicate where you passed by there house, just indicate it with an X.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: It's this area here.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if you would just turn that into an arrow to indicate your direction of travel, sir? Which direction were you heading?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if you would again just write PW-127 and today's date and then we'll be done with this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is this the front of the house or the back of the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the back, the back of the house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That makes sense otherwise can wouldn't match the other picture what he marked on the other picture. Let's move.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I want to turn your attention back to the meadow, sir. Can you give the Trial Chamber an idea of how many Serb soldiers you saw in the area of the meadow?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: There were as many as ants in an ant hill. Wherever you looked, wherever you turned your gaze, there were Serb soldiers there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you see any Serb soldiers do anything with particular Muslim prisoners who were with you in that meadow?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: Yes. I saw that two of them would take the men, they would -- I saw them take five men behind the tank to my right, behind the tank to my right there was some kind of an maize field and that's where they took the men.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If we could move into private session, just briefly, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's move into private session nor a short while.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, without referring to the names of anybody whom you just mentioned, did you see any of those people return after they had been brought away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: None of them returned while I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, has anyone seen or heard from any of those individuals since that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: From that day until three months ago, nothing was heard of them, and they never turned up anywhere. I have information that's three months old. So until three months ago, none of the individuals I've mentioned turned up alive anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Would you tell the Trial Chamber, please, what you recall happening to you next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: When we arrived on the meadow, one of the Serb soldiers told me to go to the left. That's left looking away from the road, up the meadow, to the left of the tank. So I went up there and sat down. I joined a group there. And I saw those Serb soldiers and I saw the two I had seen before asking for money, they came to the group, looking for money and jewellery, and some others. At one point, I saw a Muslim prisoner who gave a Serb soldier who was to my right about a metre or two away it to my right, he gave them 20 German marks. I remember that well.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I just want to clarify one thing, sir. You referred a moment ago to seeing the two Serb soldiers who had been asking for money earlier come back to the meadow, you've talked about two sets of soldiers who were asking for money. Could you just clarify for the Trial Chamber, please, which two Serb soldiers you saw back at the money -- back at the meadow again demanding money?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: Well, to put it more simply, after the surrender, the first encounter with the Serb soldiers, the first two we encountered, I think you'll find that I said they were sitting to my left, there was the one with two bandoliers crossed across his chest, those two came back. I mean they turned up again on the meadow. They were there asking for money.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What happened next, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: After that, a Serb soldier sitting on the tank said, "Fuck your balija mother. Get up and come here." The plan in front of me stood up and the man said, "Fuck. Your mother, not you. The one sitting behind you." I stood up and came up to the tank and he gave me two water canisters. He told me to go down to at a time asphalt road, turn left, and get some water and bring it back for the wounded. I did as instructed. I took those canisters. I went to the left. The distance was about 150 metres and there were some water there, across the road from the house, in the right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you passed by the house, first of all, are you referring to the house which you identified a few moments ago on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the same house, yes. I do apologise. I'm referring to the same house when I'm describing this.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you notice anything near the house or at the house when you were fetching the water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: There were soldiers standing around the house. I noticed, how shall I put this, a neighbour, I don't want to mention his name. They had probably separated him off before. And you could hear sounds of beating coming from the house. You could hear cries. You could hear blows. They were beating people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What did you do after you fetched the water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: I went back to the meadow. They told me to distribute the water, give everybody a little water, and that's what I did. I remember I had those two canisters and I distributed the water and then I went back to get some more water.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: At some point while you were distributing the water, did you see your father and brother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: Yes. I did. I gave my father some water to drink.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you just were testifying that you went back to fetch more water. Can you tell the Trial Chamber what happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: Waiting for the water, at one point I saw two black cars driving up, and stopping. After that, because there were three or four of us fetching water for the wounded, and we were waiting, I was approached by a Serb soldier who said, "Fuck your mother. Why are you laughing?" I said, "I'm not laughing." I didn't feel like laughing at that time. And he said, "Don't answer back." And then another soldier, who was there on my right, said, "Let the young man go. Let the boy go." I think that helped a little. So this first soldier, who had been pointing his rifle at me, left. I think the second one, who was on my right, was some kind of commander or boss. He was in charge because this first one obeyed him. When he left, there were buses coming from Potocari with women and children in them. One of them stopped nearby. The man opened the door and said, "Get some water and put it here next to the wheel." He gave me a packet to fill and he got out and talked to the Serb soldiers. There were many of them there. And I took my chance. I entered the bus and I thought I'd take my chance. I hid among some women. They put some sort of bags on top of me to conceal me. The driver spent some time talking outside. Then he got back in, switched on the engine and nobody noticed that I was hiding in the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you saw your chance to get on the bus, sir, did you let any of the Serb soldiers in the area know that you were getting on the bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: It didn't occur to me. It would have been a crazy thing to do. I tried to be as discreet as possible, to get on the bus without being observed. They would certainly have pulled me out. Maybe they would have killed me on the spot. Well, I don't know what they would have done. I won't go into details but I'm sure they wouldn't have let me board the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see we are approaching the break time. I only have a couple of short video clips and some follow-up questions and then I will conclude my examination-in-chief so I think this will be a logical time to take the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. We need a 30 minute -- we will have a 30-minute break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, please, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before you continue, one moment. One question that hasn't been asked. Was the witness ever in that place, that meadow, before in his life? Was he familiar with the area, in other words?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Witness, did you understand Mr. President's question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: Yes. I understood the question. I'd never been there before. I wasn't familiar with that place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And you wouldn't know the name of the area? Or you didn't know then, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Yes, please proceed, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Just to follow up briefly on the question, sir, have you ever returned to that area since the day you were kept prisoner in the meadow?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: Three months ago, three months ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you do that in connection with any event?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: I just had the desire to go and see, to see how I would feel after such things had happened, how I would feel if I returned to the same place.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And I guess the natural question is how did it make you feel, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: Well, it's not a great feeling, when you know that you left your father there, that he's gone, when you know that just a couple of hours before, you were in Srebrenica and how many people were buried that day. It makes your heart work hard, and all these emotions come up and then at one point you say why did I have to do that, why did you have to go see that? The whole event comes back to you. You recall everything that had happened. You are reminded of what happened there, why this had to happen, what was the reason why these people were killed, and so finally then you have one answer or no answer. My personal opinion was that because we were Muslims, they wanted to kill us all. The other thing is whether somebody wanted to do this themselves or whether this was somebody's idea. I mean, this is very sad. And for a while, after that, I really couldn't collect myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You referred to people being buried that day. Just for clarification purposes, sir, what are you referring to when you talk about people being buried that day in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: I think that on the 11th of July was the 11th anniversary of the fall of Srebrenica so I was present at the commemoration. This is what I was referring to, the people who were buried on that day, the 11th anniversary of the fall.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, I want to play you some video clips, they are all contained in the trial video, P02047. The first clip begins I believe at 02.37.42 and just to let you know, sir, we'll be jumping in and out of private session as we show you the clips.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we may go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session for a short while, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And the next clip begins at 2 hours 50 minutes 15 [sic] seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, we are at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment because we need to correct either what you said or what the transcript says. In line 5, page 70, it says you're reported as saying and the next clip begins at 2 hours 50 minutes 15 seconds. It actually started much before that and it ends at 2 minutes 50 -- 2 hours 50 minutes 18.5 seconds. So you need to state exactly when it started.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I can do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It was 2.48 or 49 or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Ms. Stewart to the rescue again, 2 hours 49 minutes and 12 seconds was the actual start time of the clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir again we are looking at the time of 2 hours 50 minutes 18.5 seconds. Do you see anything in this image and the seconds preceding it that you have testified about previously to the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: I see an UNPROFOR helmet. I saw the UNPROFOR helmet.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness's other microphone be turned on, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This helmet is identical as the ones we saw from the woods when they were patrolling in the APC.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, you're being shown an image at 2 hours 50 minutes 43.4 seconds. Do you recognise what's in this image?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: Yes. I recognise the tank which was, as I explained, on my left side as you came to the meadow. That is the tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If we may go into private session, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session for a short while, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you see an image at 2 hours 51 minutes 2.7 seconds. There is a white structure to the right of the screen. Do you recognise what that structure was from the few seconds that preceded this particular clip?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: That could be perhaps the house that we all passed by. I also recognise the bags, the rucksacks. There were a lot of them next to the house on the asphalt.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Just so the record is clear, sir, it may be a translation issue, it indicates that you testified that this could be the house. Are you uncertain about that or are you clear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, from this angle I'm not quite sure. You can hardly see anything. All I can recognise are the bags. There were a lot of such bags next to the house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's see the preceding stills at least or -- if we can see anything.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. That is the house. I've now looked at it a little better.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: May we move moo private session, Your Honour, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go back to private session again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, at 2 hours, 51 minutes 29.2 seconds you're being shown an image in the foreground there is a soldier with a weapon over his right shoulder. Do you recognise anything that this soldier is wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: Yes. I recognise in this case the UNPROFOR flak jacket. It's from UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: At 2 hours 51 seconds -- 51 minutes, 38.2 seconds. There is a group of men that are to the right of that image. Do you see that on the screen? There is a man in blue in the forefront but to the right of the image there are some men that are also depicted. Do you see that, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Just for the record to be clear, can you describe approximately where those men are located in terms of when you came out of the woods and were walking to the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: This is at the beginning, at the incline that I was talking about, and I can see that there were more people as he was filming them. When I was passing there were two of them but that is that spot. When you come out, then there is that small incline, and then you encounter them.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we may go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: With the Court's indulgence we are actually cutting out an image to save some time. We are going to move to a different one.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: May I just ask is this transmitting? No? Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's specify where we are straight away.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Beginning at 2 hours 39 minutes and 21 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir we are at 2 hours 39 minutes 45.3 seconds. Do you recognise the two individuals in this image?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: Yes. These are the two that I mentioned in my testimony earlier, they were after the first two soldiers. They were sitting and I said that they also asked for money. I remember well that I noticed the emblem on his left sleeve, the coat of arms. I also recognised him by the bandoliers.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And again, sir, at 02 hours 39 minutes 54.2 seconds, do you recognise what's depicted in that image?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: Here we can see the meadow I talked about. This is the meadow where I was. These are the people I was talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If we may just move into private session just one last time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, you testified that you discovered that your father was also at the meadow when you were passing out water to the prisoners. Did you ever see your father again after giving him a drink of water that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: That was the last time I saw my father. I never saw him again. What I regret most is that he was wounded, maybe they made him suffer although he was wounded. I don't know what happened to him. I never found out.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. One moment. I need to consult with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That is a minor technical problem that we can bypass. Witness, we are now to start with the cross-examinations. That means the various Defence teams will take it in turn and put questions to you. Can we start now or do you wish to have a break? Basically we have only got seven minutes left today. How are you feeling? Are you feeling in a way that we can --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can -- yes, Your Honour, we can continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Then Mr. Zivanovic, who is appearing for Colonel Popovic in this case, will start with his cross-examination. And he will continue tomorrow obviously.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In your testimony here, you said that Srebrenica was constantly shelled until the 10th of July. Could you please clarify whether this means that it was also shelled on the 10th of July or only up to that date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: When the shelling began, it never stopped until the morning of the 11th. On the morning of the 11th, as I said, everything was quiet and one had the impression that the madness was about to stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we go into private session for a moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go back to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: That part of Srebrenica where the petrol station is and the UNPROFOR base was, is that called Kazan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: No. It borders with that place. The petrol station is there and Kazani begins across the road from the petrol station. And then goes on. So it's all in the vicinity.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Just tell me how far is Kazan from the UNPROFOR base in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127
utterances.text: Well, it's adjacent to it, because it's adjacent to that fence where UNPROFOR was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You mean for today or --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You've finished your cross-examination. All right. I don't think there is much sense in starting the next one if we only have one minute left so we'll give you a break now, sir. You need to come back again tomorrow morning at 9.00 and I suppose that within an hour or so we'll finish your cross-examination and you will be free to go back. I thank you and we'll meet again tomorrow morning.
